## Learning goals: programming
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- **Apply** basic constructs in a programming language.
- **Analyse** data and **construct** data types to represent data.
- **Analyse** tasks and **construct** programs to carry out the tasks.

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## Learning goals: bioinformatics
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- **Describe** and **relate** central methods in bioinformatic analysis.
- **Apply** bioinformatic software to biological data.
- **Assess** the reliability of results from bioinformatic software.

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## What is programming?
<!-- ============================================================ -->

**In your head**

- To think about a problem in a structured way — like when you want to build a
lego model.
- To come up with a way to solve the problem.
- To give an unambiguous and exhaustive description of the way to solve the
problem.

**On the computer**

- To write the code.

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## What is a program?
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- A long sequence of simple instructions in a controlled order.

```{.python .large}
x = 4
y = x + 1
```

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## Pedagogical choices and omissions
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- The Python programming language.
- Only the necessary elements.
- A "layer upon layer" approach.
- Tailor-made lecture notes.
- Focus on clear and structured thinking.
- Maximal learning vs. realism in the exercises.
- Programming has to be done (a lot) to be learned.

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## The Karate Kid (1984)
<!-- ============================================================ -->

![](images/w01-s0034-1.png){.r-stretch}

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## The key to success
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- Make sure you can "see the lego bricks".
- Do not skip material. It only holds the most necessary things, so all of it
matters.
- Make sure your understanding keeps up all the way.
- The "easy stuff" must be read, understood and practised more thoroughly than
it may seem to need.
- Do not give each other solutions — give help to self-help.
- Most important: keep an eye on whether you can *find* solutions yourself — or
whether you can only *recognise* them when you are shown them.

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## My expectations of you
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- Learning by doing - and failing miserably
- Ask — especially stupid questions are important (for many others than
yourself)
- Reason — guessing and remembering will not carry you through courses.
- Be brave, experiment, try things out

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## No answer sheets…
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- There will be no answer sheets or solutions to the exercises
- You must learn how to tell whether what you made is right…

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## Python errors
<!-- ============================================================ -->

- Syntax error: when Python cannot recognize your code as Python code, it is not
run at all.
- Runtime error: a fault Python does not discover until your code runs.
- [Remember that even when your code runs fine, that is no guarantee it does what
you think it does :-)]{.alert}


<!-- ============================================================ -->

<!-- ============================================================ -->

```{.python code-line-numbers="|1|2|3"}

print "Hello"
```

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## Relational operators
<!-- ============================================================ -->

::: {.large .absolute top="15%" left="5%"}
|      |                          |
|------|--------------------------|
| `==` | equal to                 |
| `!=` | not equal to             |
| `>`  | greater than             |
| `<`  | less than                |
| `>=` | greater than or equal to |
| `<=` | less than or equal to    |
:::

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## Operator precedence
<!-- ============================================================ -->

::: {.large}
| Level   | Category       | Operators              |
|---------|----------------|------------------------|
| Highest | exponent       | `**`                   |
|         | multiplication | `*, /, //, %`          |
|         | addition       | `+, -`                 |
| Lowest  | relational     | `!=, ==, <=, >=, <, >` |
:::

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## Operator precedence
<!-- ============================================================ -->

::: {.large}
| Level   | Category       | Operators              |
|---------|----------------|------------------------|
| Highest | exponent       | `**`                   |
|         | multiplication | `*, /, //, %`          |
|         | addition       | `+, -`                 |
|         | relational     | `!=, ==, <=, >=, <, >` |
| Lowest  | logical        | `not`                  |
:::

<!-- ============================================================ -->

and     or

<!-- ============================================================ -->
## Operator precedence
<!-- ============================================================ -->

::: {.large}
| Level   | Category       | Operators              |
|---------|----------------|------------------------|
| Highest | exponent       | `**`                   |
|         | multiplication | `*, /, //, %`          |
|         | addition       | `+, -`                 |
|         | relational     | `!=, ==, <=, >=, <, >` |
|         | logical        | `not`                  |
|         | logical        | `and`                  |
| Lowest  | logical        | `or`                   |
:::

7 > 3 and 4 == 4
